chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

No, by Allah! Allah the Exalted did not intend from the people except two characteristics: that they acknowledge to Him the bounties, so He increases them, and (acknowledge) the sins, so He forgives them for them.
ai.seo_question: What are the two main things Allah desires from people according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) elucidates that divine intent for humanity rests on two reciprocal spiritual dynamics: gratitude (shukr) for blessings which invites increase, and acknowledgment of sins (which implies regret and repentance) which triggers forgiveness. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of conscious recognition—both of divine favors and of one's own shortcomings—as the primary mechanism for spiritual elevation and divine mercy.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Want from the people except for two characteristics, that he acknowledges to Him<sup>azwj</sup> of the Bounties so He<sup>azwj</sup> would Increase it for him, and (acknowledge) with the sins, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive these for him’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from those whom has mentioned (in his book) from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
By Allah, Allah, the Most High, wants two characteristics from people: to confess that He has granted them favors so He will increase them and to confess their sins so He will forgive them.”’
